The '''Norwegian Mathematical Society''' ({{langx|no|Norsk matematisk forening}}, NMF) is a professional society for mathematicians. It was formed in 1918, with [[Carl Størmer]] elected as its first president.<ref>{{cite web |title=Some History |url=http://matematikkforeningen.no:80/enghist.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071121212504/http://matematikkforeningen.no/enghist.html |archive-date=21 November 2007 |website=Norwegian Mathematical Society |accessdate=14 September 2018 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
It organizes mathematical contests and the annual  [[Abel Prize|Abel symposium]] and also awards the [[Viggo Brun]] Prize to young [[Norway|Norwegian]] [[mathematician]]s for outstanding research in mathematics, including mathematical aspects of [[information technology]], [[mathematical physics]], [[numerical analysis]], and [[computational science]].<ref>
{{cite web
 | url = https://web.matematikkforeningen.no/viggo-brun-prisen/
 | title = Norsk Matematisk Forening: Viggo Brun-Prisen
 | last =
 | first =
 | date =5 September 2018
 | website =
 | publisher =
 | access-date = 8 July 2020
 | quote = 
}}</ref> The 2018 Prize winner was Rune Gjøringbø Haugseng.<ref>
{{cite web
 | url = https://web.matematikkforeningen.no/2018/09/07/prize-winners/
 | title = Norsk Matematisk Forening: Viggo Brun Prize Winner 2018
 | last =
 | first =
 | date = 7 September 2018
 | website =
 | publisher =
 | access-date = 8 July 2020
 | quote = 
}}</ref> 
The NMF is a member of the [[International Council for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] and provides the Norwegian National Committee in the [[International Mathematical Union]].<ref>

 | url = https://web.matematikkforeningen.no/samarbeid/
